level_data.format_evidence: gm1 and so1 start with NRBF SerializedStreamHeader and contain class Save in Assembly-CSharp; field names level, pieza, positionx, positiony, positionz, fijo. Data was inspected as bytes; .NET BinaryFormatter was not executed.
level_data.interpretation: Likely puzzle layouts and solutions; field-level parsing needed to validate correspondence.

remote_assets.assessment: No Addressables catalog or separate downloaded AssetBundle manifest found. data.unity3d is the built-in Unity player archive. Absence of external game assets cannot be proven from package alone.

restoration_limits: No original C# source or managed game DLL is included; game scripts were compiled to native arm64 IL2CPP code.

No .cs, .meta or Packages/manifest.json found in the archive; original Assets GUIDs, editor-only import settings and prefab links cannot be assumed recovered from player data. Original paths of all nine built scenes are present in BuildSettings.
Recoverable serialized fields and mesh/texture/audio/animation data do not restore script method bodies, runtime generated content, third-party SDK behavior or server-side data.
A reconstructed Unity project should be described as recovered scene/assets plus script stubs unless full native method decompilation/reimplementation has been performed and validated.
